unit.title: Đọc C2
unit.summary: Tiểu luận, xã luận, tóm tắt học thuật, truyện ngắn văn chương, châm biếm và văn phong rào đón: đọc giữa các dòng.

lessons.title: Ca ngợi sự buồn chán
lessons.summary: Tiểu luận: vì sao ta nên để mình buồn chán.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Few states of mind enjoy a worse reputation than boredom. We treat it as a minor ailment, a gap to be filled as swiftly as possible, and the devices in our pockets have made filling it almost effortless. Rarely, now, does anyone wait for a bus or stand in a queue without reaching, half-consciously, for a screen.
paragraphs.vi: Ít trạng thái tinh thần nào mang tiếng xấu hơn sự buồn chán. Ta xem nó như một chứng bệnh vặt, một khoảng trống cần lấp càng nhanh càng tốt, và những thiết bị trong túi đã khiến việc lấp đầy gần như chẳng tốn sức. Giờ đây hiếm ai chờ xe buýt hay xếp hàng mà không nửa vô thức với tay lấy màn hình.

paragraphs.en: I want to suggest that this efficiency comes at a cost we have scarcely begun to reckon with. Boredom, uncomfortable as it is, functions less as an absence than as a signal: an indication that our present activity no longer engages us and that something else is wanted. Silence the signal often enough, and we may lose the capacity to hear what it was trying to tell us.
paragraphs.vi: Tôi muốn gợi ý rằng sự hiệu quả này phải trả một cái giá mà ta hầu như chưa bắt đầu tính đến. Buồn chán, dù khó chịu, vận hành không hẳn như một sự vắng mặt mà như một tín hiệu: dấu hiệu cho thấy việc ta đang làm không còn cuốn hút và ta cần điều gì khác. Dập tắt tín hiệu ấy đủ nhiều lần, ta có thể mất khả năng nghe điều nó muốn nói.

paragraphs.en: There is, moreover, a long tradition linking idle, unstructured time with creativity. The mind left to wander tends to recombine fragments of experience in unexpected ways; many people report that their best ideas arrive not at the desk but in the shower or on a long walk. Whether boredom causes such insights or merely clears space for them is difficult to establish, and I would not want to overstate the case.
paragraphs.vi: Hơn nữa, có một truyền thống lâu đời gắn thời gian rảnh rỗi, không cấu trúc với sự sáng tạo. Tâm trí được thả trôi thường kết hợp lại những mảnh trải nghiệm theo cách bất ngờ; nhiều người kể ý tưởng hay nhất đến với họ không phải ở bàn làm việc mà khi tắm hay trong một cuộc đi bộ dài. Buồn chán gây ra những khoảnh khắc loé sáng đó hay chỉ dọn chỗ cho chúng thì khó xác định, và tôi không muốn phóng đại lập luận.

paragraphs.en: Nor am I arguing that all boredom is productive. The monotony of exhausting, repetitive labor is not a creative opportunity but a burden, and it would be glib to romanticize it. My claim is narrower: that the brief, low-stakes boredom of an empty afternoon deserves to be tolerated rather than instantly cured. We might find, if we let it linger, that it was leading somewhere.
paragraphs.vi: Tôi cũng không cho rằng mọi sự buồn chán đều hữu ích. Sự đơn điệu của lao động lặp lại kiệt sức không phải cơ hội sáng tạo mà là gánh nặng, và lãng mạn hoá nó thì thật hời hợt. Lập luận của tôi hẹp hơn: sự buồn chán ngắn ngủi, chẳng hệ trọng của một buổi chiều trống trải đáng được chịu đựng thay vì lập tức chữa trị. Nếu để nó nán lại, có khi ta nhận ra nó đang dẫn ta tới đâu đó.

headings: A cautious case for wandering minds
Why repetitive work breeds creativity
A feeling we rush to get rid of
Narrowing the argument to harmless idleness
The hidden dangers of smartphone addiction
What we lose by silencing a warning
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 describes how quickly we fill boredom; paragraph 2 recasts boredom as a signal we risk no longer hearing; paragraph 3 links idle time to creativity while hedging; paragraph 4 limits the claim to brief, low-stakes boredom. Paragraph 4 rejects the idea that repetitive labor is creative, and phones are only the setting of paragraph 1, not its argument.

exercises.prompt: Which statement most accurately reflects the writer's central claim?
choices: Repetitive labor is a hidden source of creativity.
Brief, low-stakes boredom should be tolerated rather than instantly cured.
All boredom should be encouraged.
Boredom has been proved to cause creative insights.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "My claim is narrower: that the brief, low-stakes boredom of an empty afternoon deserves to be tolerated rather than instantly cured." The same paragraph rejects romanticizing repetitive labor, and paragraph 3 refuses to claim proof.

exercises.prompt: What does the writer imply by saying that people reach for a screen "half-consciously"?
choices: People feel ashamed of being bored in public.
Screens are making people less intelligent.
Most people wait for buses impatiently.
Filling boredom has become a habit rather than a deliberate choice.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the reach for a screen happens "half-consciously" and almost without effort, so it is closer to a reflex than a decision. Shame and intelligence are not mentioned.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer add "I would not want to overstate the case" in paragraph 3?
choices: To admit that the creativity argument is false
To acknowledge that the link between boredom and creativity is uncertain
To dismiss the reports of people who have ideas in the shower
To suggest that unstructured time is harmful
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: whether boredom "causes such insights or merely clears space for them is difficult to establish". The writer still supports the link but limits how strongly it is claimed — a hedge, not a retraction.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "glib" is closest in meaning to …
choices: cruel
illegal
superficial
nostalgic
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: it would be "glib to romanticize" exhausting, repetitive labor — that is, too easy and shallow, ignoring that such work is "a burden".

exercises.statement: The writer states that boredom has been proven to cause creative insights.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: whether boredom causes insights or merely clears space for them "is difficult to establish".

exercises.statement: The writer accepts that boredom is an unpleasant experience.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "Boredom, uncomfortable as it is, functions less as an absence than as a signal."

exercises.statement: The writer has given up using a smartphone.
exercises.explain: The passage never describes the writer's own phone habits.

exercises.prompt: Many people report that their best ideas arrive in the shower or on a long ___.
choices: walk
flight
call
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "in the shower or on a long walk".

exercises.text: Boredom is usually treated as a problem to be ___ at once, and phones make that effortless. The writer argues that it is better understood as a ___ that our current activity has stopped engaging us. Unstructured time may also encourage ___, although the writer admits this is hard to prove. The claim is deliberately ___: exhausting, repetitive work is excluded.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: boredom is "a gap to be filled as swiftly as possible"; paragraph 2: it functions "as a signal"; paragraph 3: idle time is linked with creativity, but the causal link is "difficult to establish"; paragraph 4: "My claim is narrower" and repetitive labor is not included.

lessons.title: Khi con số thành ông chủ
lessons.summary: Xã luận: chỉ số đo lường bóp méo điều nó đo.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

blocks.title: When the Measure Becomes the Target

paragraphs.en: There is an old observation among economists, so frequently confirmed that it has acquired the status of a law: once a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Nowhere is this more evident than in the modern enthusiasm for performance indicators, which have spread from factories into hospitals, schools, universities and public administration.
paragraphs.vi: Có một nhận xét cũ trong giới kinh tế, được xác nhận thường xuyên đến mức gần như thành định luật: khi một thước đo trở thành mục tiêu, nó không còn là thước đo tốt. Không đâu điều này rõ hơn trong cơn hăng hái hiện đại với các chỉ số hiệu suất, vốn đã lan từ nhà máy sang bệnh viện, trường học, đại học và bộ máy hành chính công.

paragraphs.en: The logic of such indicators is superficially compelling. Public money should be spent responsibly; responsibility requires accountability; accountability requires numbers. Who could object? The trouble begins when the numbers, rather than the purposes they were meant to reflect, become the object of everyone's effort.
paragraphs.vi: Logic của những chỉ số này thoạt nghe rất thuyết phục. Tiền công phải được chi có trách nhiệm; trách nhiệm đòi hỏi giải trình; giải trình đòi hỏi con số. Ai có thể phản đối? Rắc rối bắt đầu khi chính con số, thay vì mục đích mà chúng được tạo ra để phản ánh, trở thành đối tượng của mọi nỗ lực.

paragraphs.en: Consider a hospital rewarded for reducing waiting times in its emergency department. Staff may genuinely work faster, but they may also discover that the clock stops when a patient is formally admitted, and so admit patients to a corridor. A school judged on examination pass rates may quietly discourage weaker students from sitting the exam at all. In each case the figure improves while the underlying reality stays the same, or deteriorates.
paragraphs.vi: Hãy xem một bệnh viện được thưởng vì giảm thời gian chờ ở khoa cấp cứu. Nhân viên có thể thực sự làm nhanh hơn, nhưng họ cũng có thể phát hiện đồng hồ dừng khi bệnh nhân được nhập viện chính thức, và thế là nhập bệnh nhân ra hành lang. Một trường học bị đánh giá theo tỷ lệ đỗ có thể lặng lẽ khuyên học sinh yếu đừng dự thi. Trong mỗi trường hợp, con số đẹp lên trong khi thực tế bên dưới giữ nguyên, hoặc tệ đi.

paragraphs.en: None of this is an argument against measurement as such. Numbers can reveal problems that anecdote conceals, and abandoning them would merely return us to rule by impression. The point, rather, is that indicators should inform professional judgment, not replace it. Measure, by all means, but measure several things, change the measures before they are mastered, and never mistake the map for the territory.
paragraphs.vi: Không điều gì ở trên là lập luận chống lại việc đo lường nói chung. Con số có thể phơi bày vấn đề mà giai thoại che giấu, và từ bỏ chúng chỉ đưa ta về lối cai quản bằng cảm tính. Ý chính là chỉ số nên cung cấp thông tin cho phán đoán chuyên môn, chứ không thay thế nó. Cứ đo lường, nhưng hãy đo nhiều thứ, thay đổi thước đo trước khi người ta thành thạo việc lách nó, và đừng bao giờ nhầm bản đồ với lãnh thổ.

headings: Using numbers wisely rather than abandoning them
How hospitals reduced emergency waiting times
A persuasive chain of reasoning, and where it goes wrong
An economic law and its spread into public life
Why anecdotes are more reliable than statistics
Cases where the figures improve but the service does not
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 states the law and the spread of indicators; paragraph 2 sets out the appealing logic and where trouble begins; paragraph 3 gives the hospital and school examples; paragraph 4 defends measurement used with judgment. Paragraph 3 shows waiting-time figures improving without real change, and paragraph 4 says numbers reveal what anecdote conceals.

exercises.prompt: What does the hospital example illustrate?
choices: Hospitals are generally inefficient.
Staff always work faster when rewarded.
Waiting times cannot be measured accurately.
A figure can improve while the underlying reality does not.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: admitting patients to a corridor stops the clock, so "the figure improves while the underlying reality stays the same, or deteriorates".

exercises.prompt: What does the question "Who could object?" in paragraph 2 suggest?
choices: The writer fully accepts the case for performance indicators.
Nobody has ever criticized performance indicators.
The writer is about to challenge reasoning that seems hard to dispute.
Public money is usually spent irresponsibly.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the logic is only "superficially compelling", and the next sentence begins "The trouble begins…". The question voices the obvious reaction so that the writer can then show its weakness.

exercises.prompt: What does the writer mean by "never mistake the map for the territory"?
choices: Indicators should always be presented visually.
A measurement is only a simplified picture of the reality it describes.
Local knowledge matters more than national policy.
Professionals should visit the places they manage.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: the metaphor closes the argument that indicators should inform judgment, not replace it. As a map is not the land itself, a number is not the purpose it was meant to reflect (paragraph 2).

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "mastered" is closest in meaning to …
choices: officially approved
learned well enough to be exploited
completely forgotten
widely published
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "change the measures before they are mastered" — before people learn how to improve the number without improving the reality, as in the corridor and exam examples of paragraph 3.

exercises.statement: The writer argues against all forms of measurement.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "None of this is an argument against measurement as such."

exercises.statement: The writer thinks that relying on impressions alone would be worse than using numbers.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: numbers reveal problems that anecdote conceals, and abandoning them "would merely return us to rule by impression".

exercises.statement: The writer works in a hospital emergency department.
exercises.explain: The hospital is only an example in paragraph 3; the writer's own job is never mentioned.

exercises.prompt: A school judged on pass rates may discourage weaker students from ___ the exam.
choices: sitting
grading
setting
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "discourage weaker students from sitting the exam" (sit an exam = dự thi).

exercises.text: Once a number is turned into a ___, people begin working to improve the number itself rather than the purpose behind it. A hospital may move patients into corridors and a school may keep weaker students away from exams, so that the figures look better while real ___ does not. The writer does not reject measurement but wants it to support professional ___, using several indicators that are ___ before people learn to game them.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: "once a measure becomes a target"; paragraph 3: the figure improves while the underlying reality does not; paragraph 4: indicators should "inform professional judgment", and measures should be changed "before they are mastered".

lessons.title: Tóm tắt nghiên cứu: chuyển mã ngôn ngữ
lessons.summary: Đọc văn phong tóm tắt học thuật (abstract).

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

blocks.title: Abstract: Code-Switching and Identity Among Bilingual Adolescents

paragraphs.en: Background. Code-switching, the alternation between two or more languages within a single conversation, has traditionally been interpreted either as evidence of incomplete proficiency or as a purely pragmatic strategy for filling lexical gaps. A growing body of sociolinguistic research suggests, however, that it may also serve as a resource for constructing and negotiating social identity.
paragraphs.vi: Bối cảnh. Chuyển mã, tức việc luân phiên giữa hai hay nhiều ngôn ngữ trong cùng một cuộc hội thoại, theo truyền thống được diễn giải hoặc là bằng chứng của năng lực chưa hoàn thiện, hoặc là chiến lược thuần thực dụng để lấp khoảng trống từ vựng. Tuy nhiên, ngày càng nhiều nghiên cứu ngôn ngữ học xã hội gợi ý rằng nó cũng có thể là nguồn lực để kiến tạo và thương lượng bản sắc xã hội.

paragraphs.en: Method. The present study examined naturally occurring conversations among 48 bilingual adolescents, aged 14 to 17, recorded over six months in school and leisure settings. Switches were coded according to their apparent function, and participants subsequently took part in semi-structured interviews in which they commented on selected extracts of their own speech.
paragraphs.vi: Phương pháp. Nghiên cứu này khảo sát các cuộc hội thoại tự nhiên của 48 thiếu niên song ngữ từ 14 đến 17 tuổi, được ghi âm trong sáu tháng ở môi trường trường học và giải trí. Các lần chuyển mã được mã hoá theo chức năng biểu hiện, sau đó người tham gia dự phỏng vấn bán cấu trúc, bình luận về những trích đoạn chọn lọc từ chính lời nói của mình.

paragraphs.en: Results. Contrary to the deficit hypothesis, the majority of switches occurred at points where an equivalent expression was readily available in the language being spoken. Switches clustered around jokes, expressions of solidarity and moments of disagreement. In interviews, participants frequently described switching as a way of signaling closeness to peers or distance from adult authority, although several also reported doing so without conscious intention.
paragraphs.vi: Kết quả. Trái với giả thuyết thiếu hụt, phần lớn lần chuyển mã xảy ra ở chỗ mà ngôn ngữ đang nói sẵn có cách diễn đạt tương đương. Chuyển mã tập trung quanh lời đùa, biểu hiện đoàn kết và lúc bất đồng. Trong phỏng vấn, người tham gia thường mô tả chuyển mã như cách báo hiệu sự thân thiết với bạn bè hoặc giữ khoảng cách với quyền uy người lớn, dù một số cũng cho biết họ làm vậy mà không có chủ ý.

paragraphs.en: Conclusions. These findings indicate that, for this population, code-switching functions predominantly as a social rather than a compensatory resource. Given the modest sample and its restriction to a single urban community, generalization should be undertaken with caution; further research across different age groups and language pairings is warranted.
paragraphs.vi: Kết luận. Các phát hiện này cho thấy, với nhóm đối tượng này, chuyển mã chủ yếu đóng vai trò nguồn lực xã hội hơn là bù đắp. Do mẫu nhỏ và chỉ giới hạn trong một cộng đồng đô thị, cần thận trọng khi khái quát hoá; cần thêm nghiên cứu ở các nhóm tuổi và cặp ngôn ngữ khác.

headings: How the speech data were collected and analyzed
Evidence that bilingual teenagers lack vocabulary
A cautious interpretation and a call for more work
Language switches as social signals
Differences between language use at school and at home
Competing explanations for mixing languages
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 (Background) contrasts traditional explanations with the identity view; paragraph 2 (Method) describes recordings, coding and interviews; paragraph 3 (Results) shows switches marking jokes, solidarity, closeness and distance; paragraph 4 (Conclusions) interprets the results cautiously. The results contradict a lack of vocabulary, and school and leisure settings are never compared.

exercises.prompt: Which finding contradicts the "deficit hypothesis"?
choices: Participants were aged 14 to 17.
Most switches occurred where an equivalent expression was available.
Conversations were recorded for six months.
Some participants switched without conscious intention.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "Contrary to the deficit hypothesis, the majority of switches occurred at points where an equivalent expression was readily available", so speakers were not switching because they lacked the words.

exercises.prompt: Why did the researchers most likely ask participants to comment on extracts of their own speech?
choices: To test their proficiency in both languages
To compare the speakers' own accounts with the functions the researchers had coded
To teach them to avoid unnecessary switching
To record more natural conversations
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: switches were first coded by "apparent function", and participants "subsequently" commented on extracts; paragraph 3 then reports how participants themselves described switching. The interviews add the speakers' view to the researchers' coding; the natural conversations had already been recorded.

exercises.prompt: What does the report that several participants switched "without conscious intention" suggest?
choices: Those participants were less proficient than the others.
The recordings for those participants were unreliable.
Speakers' own explanations may not account for every switch.
Switching is never a social act.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: most participants described switching as signaling closeness or distance, "although several also reported doing so without conscious intention". So not every switch can be explained by what speakers say they intend, though the study still sees switching as mainly social (paragraph 4).

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word "warranted" is closest in meaning to …
choices: guaranteed
forbidden
justified
funded
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: because the sample is modest and limited to one community, "further research … is warranted" — there is good reason for it. "Guaranteed" confuses the word with "warranty".

exercises.statement: All participants said they switched languages deliberately.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: several reported switching "without conscious intention".

exercises.statement: Switches tended to occur at socially significant moments rather than at random.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: switches "clustered around jokes, expressions of solidarity and moments of disagreement".

exercises.statement: Girls in the study switched languages more often than boys.
exercises.explain: The abstract gives no results by gender.

exercises.prompt: The study concludes that code-switching functions mainly as a social rather than a ___ resource.
choices: compensatory
linguistic
academic
exercises.explain: Đoạn Conclusions: "a social rather than a compensatory resource".

exercises.text: Code-switching has often been explained either as a sign of limited ___ or as a practical way to fill gaps in vocabulary. This study of 48 bilingual teenagers found that most switches happened even when the current language offered a suitable ___. Switching appeared to signal closeness to friends or ___ from adults. Since the sample came from a single urban community, the authors urge ___ before generalizing.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: switching was seen as "incomplete proficiency" or a way of filling lexical gaps; paragraph 3: an equivalent expression was usually available, and switching signaled closeness to peers or "distance from adult authority"; paragraph 4: "generalization should be undertaken with caution".

lessons.title: Con gái người vẽ bản đồ
lessons.summary: Truyện ngắn: đọc ẩn ý và hình ảnh.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: My father drew maps for a living, though by the time I was old enough to understand what that meant, the work had largely passed to satellites and software. He kept at it anyway, in a narrow room at the top of the house, bent over sheets of paper so large that they curled at the edges like something trying to escape.
paragraphs.vi: Cha tôi vẽ bản đồ để kiếm sống, dù lúc tôi đủ lớn để hiểu điều đó nghĩa là gì thì công việc phần lớn đã chuyển sang vệ tinh và phần mềm. Ông vẫn miệt mài, trong căn phòng hẹp trên tầng cao nhất của ngôi nhà, cúi xuống những tờ giấy lớn đến mức mép giấy cong lên như thứ gì đó đang muốn trốn thoát.

paragraphs.en: He was not, I think, unaware of his own obsolescence. When clients stopped calling, he began mapping places no one had asked for: the creek behind the school, our street as it had looked before the new houses, the route my mother used to walk to the station. He labeled everything in a small, upright hand, as if precision might compensate for the fact that nobody would ever consult these maps to find their way.
paragraphs.vi: Tôi nghĩ ông không phải không biết mình đã lỗi thời. Khi khách hàng thôi gọi, ông bắt đầu vẽ những nơi chẳng ai yêu cầu: con lạch sau trường học, con phố nhà tôi như nó từng trông trước khi có những ngôi nhà mới, lộ trình mẹ tôi từng đi bộ ra ga. Ông ghi chú mọi thứ bằng nét chữ nhỏ, thẳng đứng, như thể sự chính xác có thể bù lại việc sẽ chẳng ai tra những tấm bản đồ này để tìm đường.

paragraphs.en: It was only after he died that I understood they had never been meant for finding anything. Spread across the floor of his room, the sheets fitted together into a single, enormous plan of the town, but a town that no longer existed: the cinema that had become a parking lot, the bakery where my mother had worked, the bench where, according to a tiny note in the margin, he had first spoken to her.
paragraphs.vi: Chỉ sau khi ông mất tôi mới hiểu chúng chưa bao giờ được làm ra để tìm thứ gì. Trải khắp sàn phòng ông, những tờ giấy ghép lại thành một bản đồ khổng lồ duy nhất của thị trấn, nhưng là một thị trấn không còn tồn tại: rạp chiếu phim nay thành bãi đỗ xe, tiệm bánh nơi mẹ tôi từng làm, chiếc ghế dài nơi, theo một dòng ghi chú nhỏ bên lề, ông lần đầu nói chuyện với bà.

paragraphs.en: I have them still, rolled in a cupboard. Occasionally I take one out and trace a road with my finger, and it occurs to me that he was the most accurate cartographer I have ever known, if accuracy is measured not by distance but by what was lost.
paragraphs.vi: Tôi vẫn giữ chúng, cuộn lại trong tủ. Thỉnh thoảng tôi lấy một tờ ra, lấy ngón tay dò theo một con đường, và chợt nghĩ ông là người vẽ bản đồ chính xác nhất tôi từng biết, nếu sự chính xác được đo không phải bằng khoảng cách mà bằng những gì đã mất.

headings: A new way of judging precision
The father's struggle to find new clients
Mapping places nobody had asked for
How the town was rebuilt
Holding on to a craft that technology had replaced
The hidden purpose of the maps revealed
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 shows the father continuing mapmaking after satellites and software took over; paragraph 2 describes the unrequested personal maps; paragraph 3 reveals after his death that they form a lost town; paragraph 4 redefines accuracy as measuring what was lost. Paragraph 2 says clients stopped calling, not that he looked for new ones, and the rebuilding of the town is never described.

exercises.prompt: What did the narrator realize about the father's later maps after his death?
choices: They were meant to record a town that no longer existed.
They were commissioned by the town council.
They contained serious errors.
They were copies of satellite images.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: spread out, the sheets formed a single plan of "a town that no longer existed", so they "had never been meant for finding anything".

exercises.prompt: What does the final sentence suggest?
choices: The father measured distances more carefully than anyone.
The narrator wants to become a cartographer.
The maps' true value lay in preserving memory and loss.
The narrator plans to sell the maps.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: he was the most accurate cartographer "if accuracy is measured not by distance but by what was lost" — the maps faithfully recorded a vanished past, not physical distances.

exercises.prompt: What does the narrator suggest about the father's careful labeling in paragraph 2?
choices: It was required by his former clients.
It helped strangers find their way around the town.
It may have been a way of giving value to maps that no one would use.
It shows that he hoped to sell the maps.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: he labeled everything precisely "as if precision might compensate for the fact that nobody would ever consult these maps". These maps were of places "no one had asked for", so clients did not require them, and no one used them to find the way.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "obsolescence" is closest in meaning to …
choices: great age
being out of date
poor health
loneliness
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: right after "his own obsolescence" we read that "clients stopped calling" — his skill was no longer needed now that mapmaking had passed to satellites and software (paragraph 1). It refers to his work, not his age.

exercises.statement: The father continued drawing maps even after most of the work had passed to technology.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the work had largely passed to satellites and software, but "He kept at it anyway".

exercises.statement: The father's later maps were made at the request of local clients.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: when clients stopped calling, he mapped "places no one had asked for".

exercises.statement: The narrator's mother was born in the same town as the father.
exercises.explain: The story never says where either parent was born.

exercises.prompt: The cinema in the town had become a parking ___.
choices: lot
garden
school
exercises.explain: Đoạn 3: "the cinema that had become a parking lot".

exercises.text: The narrator's father was a mapmaker whose trade had largely been taken over by ___. When work dried up, he drew places of personal ___ instead. Only after his death did the narrator see that the sheets formed one map of a town that had ___, recording what had been ___ rather than how to find the way.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: the work passed to satellites and software; paragraph 2: he mapped the creek, the old street and the mother's route; paragraph 3: the sheets showed "a town that no longer existed"; paragraph 4: accuracy measured "by what was lost".

lessons.title: Cẩm nang năng suất "khiêm tốn"
lessons.summary: Châm biếm: nhận ra giọng mỉa mai.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

blocks.title: A Modest Guide to Total Productivity

paragraphs.en: Congratulations on deciding to become maximally productive. You have doubtless noticed that ordinary people waste vast quantities of time on unprofitable activities such as sleeping, eating slowly and talking to friends without a clearly defined agenda. This guide will help you eliminate such inefficiencies once and for all.
paragraphs.vi: Chúc mừng bạn đã quyết định trở nên năng suất tối đa. Hẳn bạn đã nhận thấy người bình thường phí phạm vô số thời gian vào những hoạt động không sinh lời như ngủ, ăn chậm và trò chuyện với bạn bè mà không có chương trình nghị sự rõ ràng. Cẩm nang này sẽ giúp bạn loại bỏ những sự kém hiệu quả ấy một lần cho mãi mãi.

paragraphs.en: Begin each morning at four o'clock, a time favored by the highly successful, or at least by those who write books about the highly successful. Before your feet touch the floor, review your goals for the day, the year and the decade. Should you feel tired, remind yourself that fatigue is merely a lack of discipline that has not yet been optimized.
paragraphs.vi: Hãy bắt đầu mỗi sáng lúc bốn giờ, giờ được những người cực kỳ thành công ưa chuộng, hoặc ít nhất là được những người viết sách về người cực kỳ thành công ưa chuộng. Trước khi chân chạm sàn, hãy rà lại mục tiêu của ngày, của năm và của cả thập kỷ. Nếu thấy mệt, hãy tự nhắc rằng mệt mỏi chỉ là sự thiếu kỷ luật chưa được tối ưu hoá.

paragraphs.en: Leisure, of course, need not be abandoned entirely; it must simply be made useful. Listen to instructional recordings at double speed while exercising. Read only books that can be summarized in a single slide. If you must see your family, schedule the meeting in advance and circulate minutes afterward so that action points are not forgotten.
paragraphs.vi: Dĩ nhiên không cần bỏ hẳn thời gian rảnh; chỉ cần biến nó thành hữu ích. Nghe bản ghi hướng dẫn ở tốc độ gấp đôi khi tập thể dục. Chỉ đọc những cuốn sách có thể tóm tắt trong một trang trình chiếu. Nếu buộc phải gặp gia đình, hãy lên lịch trước và gửi biên bản sau đó để không quên các đầu việc.

paragraphs.en: Follow these principles faithfully and you will soon achieve a state of perfect efficiency, in which every minute is accounted for and none of them is enjoyed. At that point you may at last pause and ask what all the time you saved was for, though we recommend scheduling that question for a later quarter.
paragraphs.vi: Tuân thủ trung thành các nguyên tắc này và bạn sẽ sớm đạt trạng thái hiệu quả hoàn hảo, trong đó mỗi phút đều được tính toán và chẳng phút nào được tận hưởng. Lúc ấy cuối cùng bạn có thể dừng lại và tự hỏi tất cả thời gian tiết kiệm được để làm gì, dù chúng tôi khuyên nên xếp câu hỏi đó vào một quý sau.

headings: Turning free time and family into work
The scientific case for waking early
An invitation to cut out ordinary pleasures
Efficiency achieved, purpose forgotten
Tips for eating more healthily
A punishing start to the day
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 invites the reader to eliminate sleep, slow meals and friendship; paragraph 2 prescribes a four o'clock start; paragraph 3 makes leisure and family "useful"; paragraph 4 describes joyless efficiency and the postponed question of purpose. No scientific evidence is offered for waking early, and eating slowly is mentioned only as a "waste".

exercises.prompt: What is the writer's real attitude toward the advice given?
choices: Enthusiastic support
Neutral description
Scientific evaluation
Ironic criticism of an obsessive productivity culture
exercises.explain: The satire runs through every paragraph, for example scheduling family "meetings" with minutes (paragraph 3) and a perfect efficiency in which no minute "is enjoyed" (paragraph 4), so the writer is mocking the advice, not recommending it.

exercises.prompt: What is implied by the phrase "or at least by those who write books about the highly successful"?
choices: Successful people never write books.
The claim about four o'clock may come more from productivity authors than from successful people themselves.
Writing books is the best way to become successful.
All successful people wake up at four o'clock.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: the afterthought undercuts the claim — the evidence for the four o'clock habit may be the books, not the successful people.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer describe sleeping, eating slowly and talking to friends as "unprofitable activities"?
choices: To recommend that readers give them up
To show that these activities cost money
To mock a mindset that values only measurable output
To criticize people who sleep too much
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: calling basic human needs and friendship "unprofitable" applies business language where it plainly does not belong. In a satire this exposes the absurd values of productivity culture rather than sincerely advising readers.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "circulate" is closest in meaning to …
choices: rewrite
distribute
discuss
file
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "circulate minutes afterward so that action points are not forgotten" — send the notes round to everyone, as after a business meeting.

exercises.prompt: What does the final suggestion to schedule the question "for a later quarter" imply?
choices: The writer plans to publish a follow-up guide.
Reflection is best done at the end of a financial year.
The question of purpose is unimportant.
The productivity mindset keeps postponing the question of what all the efficiency is for.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: even the most important question — "what all the time you saved was for" — is pushed into the schedule, so the system never stops long enough to ask why it exists. The joke presents the question as essential and endlessly delayed.

exercises.statement: The guide tells readers to send out minutes after a meeting with their family.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "circulate minutes afterward" — the guide does give this instruction, even though the advice is satirical.

exercises.statement: The writer has published several other productivity guides.
exercises.explain: The passage says nothing about the writer's other work.

exercises.prompt: Fatigue is described as a lack of discipline that has not yet been ___.
choices: optimized
measured
forgiven
exercises.explain: Đoạn 2: "a lack of discipline that has not yet been optimized".

exercises.text: Written as a cheerful self-help guide, the text is in fact a ___ of extreme productivity culture. It treats sleep and friendship as ___, recommends rising at four, and even suggests running family visits like business ___. Its final point is that a life in which every minute is used may contain no ___, and leaves no time to ask what the saved time is for.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: sleeping and talking to friends are "inefficiencies"; paragraph 3: family visits are scheduled with minutes; paragraph 4: every minute is accounted for "and none of them is enjoyed". The ironic tone throughout makes the whole text a satire.

lessons.title: Trí nhớ là sự tái dựng
lessons.summary: Văn khoa học rào đón: đọc mức độ chắc chắn.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: It is tempting to imagine memory as a kind of archive, in which experiences are stored intact and later retrieved, much as one might replay a recording. The weight of experimental evidence, however, points toward a rather different model. Remembering appears to be less an act of retrieval than one of reconstruction, in which the brain reassembles an event from scattered fragments and fills the gaps with plausible inference.
paragraphs.vi: Thật dễ hình dung trí nhớ như một kho lưu trữ, nơi trải nghiệm được cất giữ nguyên vẹn rồi được lấy ra sau, giống như phát lại một bản ghi. Tuy nhiên, phần lớn bằng chứng thực nghiệm chỉ về một mô hình khá khác. Hồi tưởng dường như không hẳn là hành động truy xuất mà là tái dựng, trong đó não lắp ghép lại sự kiện từ những mảnh rời rạc và lấp khoảng trống bằng suy luận hợp lý.

paragraphs.en: One consequence is that memories may be altered by information encountered after the event. In a number of studies, participants who were exposed to subtly misleading questions later reported details that had not in fact occurred, often with considerable confidence. Confidence, it seems, is at best a loose guide to accuracy.
paragraphs.vi: Một hệ quả là ký ức có thể bị thay đổi bởi thông tin tiếp nhận sau sự kiện. Trong một số nghiên cứu, người tham gia bị hỏi những câu gây hiểu lầm tinh vi về sau kể lại những chi tiết thực ra không xảy ra, thường với sự tự tin đáng kể. Có vẻ như sự tự tin, cùng lắm, chỉ là chỉ dấu lỏng lẻo về độ chính xác.

paragraphs.en: It would be a mistake, though, to conclude that memory is generally untrustworthy. The core of most everyday memories is probably reasonably accurate; distortions tend to affect peripheral details more than the central gist. Moreover, some researchers argue that a flexible, reconstructive system may be adaptive, allowing past experience to be recombined in order to imagine and plan for the future.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên, sẽ là sai lầm nếu kết luận rằng trí nhớ nói chung không đáng tin. Phần cốt lõi của hầu hết ký ức thường ngày có lẽ khá chính xác; sự méo mó thường ảnh hưởng đến chi tiết ngoại vi hơn là ý chính. Hơn nữa, một số nhà nghiên cứu cho rằng một hệ thống linh hoạt, mang tính tái dựng có thể có lợi cho thích nghi, cho phép kết hợp lại trải nghiệm quá khứ để hình dung và lập kế hoạch cho tương lai.

paragraphs.en: The practical implications are nonetheless significant, particularly where single recollections carry great weight, as in eyewitness testimony. Here, the evidence would seem to favor procedures that minimize suggestion, such as recording an account as early as possible and avoiding leading questions.
paragraphs.vi: Dù vậy, hệ quả thực tiễn vẫn đáng kể, nhất là khi một hồi ức đơn lẻ có sức nặng lớn, như lời khai nhân chứng. Ở đây bằng chứng dường như ủng hộ các quy trình giảm thiểu sự gợi ý, như ghi lại lời kể càng sớm càng tốt và tránh câu hỏi dẫn dắt.

headings: Practical consequences for eyewitness accounts
Techniques for improving everyday memory
From archive to rebuilding: a new model of memory
Why memory remains broadly reliable, and even useful
The link between confidence and intelligence
How later information can rewrite the past
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 replaces the archive model with reconstruction; paragraph 2 shows memories altered by misleading questions; paragraph 3 argues against concluding that memory is untrustworthy and notes its adaptive value; paragraph 4 draws implications for eyewitness testimony. The passage gives no memory-improvement techniques and does not link confidence to intelligence.

exercises.prompt: Based on paragraph 2, what can be inferred about a witness who is very sure of a detail?
choices: They are probably lying.
Their certainty alone is not good evidence that the detail is correct.
Their memory cannot have been influenced by questions.
They must have seen the event directly.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: participants reported details that never occurred "often with considerable confidence", and confidence is "at best a loose guide to accuracy". Certainty therefore cannot confirm a detail on its own, but it does not mean the witness is lying.

exercises.prompt: What is the main function of paragraph 3?
choices: To present new evidence that memory is unreliable
To explain how eyewitness procedures work
To prevent the reader from drawing an overly negative conclusion
To reject the reconstructive model of memory
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3 opens "It would be a mistake, though, to conclude that memory is generally untrustworthy", then argues that the core of memories is probably accurate and that reconstruction may be adaptive. It qualifies the reconstructive model; it does not reject it.

exercises.prompt: The phrase "would seem to favor" in paragraph 4 shows that the writer …
choices: considers the evidence conclusive
rejects the procedures mentioned
is quoting eyewitnesses directly
presents the recommendation tentatively rather than as settled fact
exercises.explain: Paragraph 4: "the evidence would seem to favor procedures that minimize suggestion" — the double hedge ("would", "seem") supports the procedures but stops short of claiming certainty, in line with the cautious tone of the whole passage.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "peripheral" is closest in meaning to …
choices: visual
invented
secondary
recent
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: distortions affect "peripheral details more than the central gist" — the contrast with "central" shows that peripheral details are the minor ones at the edges of a memory.

exercises.statement: The writer concludes that memory is generally untrustworthy.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "It would be a mistake … to conclude that memory is generally untrustworthy."

exercises.statement: According to some researchers, the flexibility of memory may bring advantages.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: some researchers argue a reconstructive system "may be adaptive", helping us imagine and plan for the future.

exercises.statement: Memory distortions are more common in older adults.
exercises.explain: The passage never mentions age.

exercises.prompt: The evidence would seem to favor avoiding ___ questions with eyewitnesses.
choices: leading
short
written
exercises.explain: Đoạn 4: "avoiding leading questions" (câu hỏi dẫn dắt).

exercises.text: Rather than replaying stored ___, the brain seems to rebuild each memory from fragments, filling the gaps with reasonable guesses. Misleading information met after an event can therefore ___ what people recall, and confidence says little about accuracy. Even so, the ___ of most memories is probably sound, and a flexible system may help us plan. Where a single account matters greatly, as with eyewitnesses, interviewers should keep ___ to a minimum.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: memory is not like replaying "a recording" but a reconstruction; paragraph 2: memories "may be altered by information encountered after the event"; paragraph 3: "the core of most everyday memories is probably reasonably accurate"; paragraph 4: procedures should "minimize suggestion".
